title: introduce-node-lifecycle-and-convergent-tfstate-mapping
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds a new gpu-node-lifecycle Terraform module that provides CA-compatible lifecycle hooks (pre-drain/post-drain), introduces an immutable subnet aliasing approach to enable seamless nodepool upgrades, and a convergent tfstate mapping helper module to safely partition state per-tenant without changing existing backends. Includes migration guide and automated plan checks.
description:
Context: Private deployments experience operational friction during nodepool upgrades and state reorganizations. Existing PRs reorganize tfstate boundaries and GPU pools but we still observe painful in-place upgrades (evictions, IAM role blips) and one-off state migration scripts. This PR provides two complementary primitives: (1) a gpu-node-lifecycle module that injects controlled drain/cordon hooks, taint choreography, and an optional broker sidecar to coordinate cross-az rolling upgrades; (2) a convergent-tfstate-mapping helper that builds a deterministic tfstate key namespace and a migration plan that can be applied incrementally with zero-downtime.

Goals: reduce outage risk during GPU nodepool upgrades, enable tenant-scoped state partitions without manual state copy steps, and unify IAM bootstrap roles for cross-account node access.

What I changed (high-level):
- New module: modules/gpu-node-lifecycle/ - implements node lifecycle resources: kubernetes daemonset for drain-agent, optional Lambda-like pre-drain hook (for cloud-managed), lifecycle scripts for on-prem installer, and sample systemd unit for air-gapped installs.
- New module: modules/tfstate-convergent-map/ - deterministic mapping of existing resources to new state keys, dry-run plan generator, and plan-check automation that fails CI if mapping would cause resource replacement without explicit opt-in.
- IAM: modules/iam/tenant-proxy-roles.tf - small refactor to introduce a tenant-proxy role that is assumed by the lifecycle broker during upgrades, reduces need for cross-account instance-role churn.
- Networking: modules/network/subnet-alias.tf - introduces the concept of immutable subnet aliases (alias resources that point to the underlying subnet id) so workloads can reference alias outputs that remain stable during subnet replacement/rehoming.
- Examples: examples/private-migration/ - a step-by-step migration example and a plan-evaluator script (python) that outputs a safe execution plan.

Commits (summary):
- 6 commits: "init gpu-node-lifecycle module" -> "add drain-agent daemonset + systemd shim" -> "tfstate-convergent-map initial implementation" -> "tenant-proxy role + tests" -> "subnet alias outputs + docs" -> "migration guide + CI plan-check"

Files changed (selected):
- modules/gpu-node-lifecycle/main.tf (new)
- modules/gpu-node-lifecycle/README.md (new)
- modules/gpu-node-lifecycle/templates/drain-agent.yaml.tpl (new)
- modules/tfstate-convergent-map/main.tf (new)
- modules/tfstate-convergent-map/plan-checker.py (new)
- modules/iam/roles.tf (modified)
- modules/network/subnet-alias.tf (new)
- examples/private-migration/README.md (new)
- examples/private-migration/plan-evaluator.py (new)

Motivation and design notes:
- Node lifecycle broker: Running rolling GPU node upgrades is tricky because of long pod restart times and KV cache warmups. The broker coordinates a pipeline: mark node unschedulable -> invoke pre-drain hook to instruct inference runtime to flush prefixes -> wait for KV cache checkpoint -> cordon/drain -> post-drain hook to resume. For cloud installs this uses short-lived functions; for on-prem the module provides a systemd shim + templates.
- Convergent tfstate mapping: Instead of migrating state by hand, the module computes a canonical key path based on cluster identifiers, tenant id, and resource fingerprint. The plan-checker simulates a migration and reports whether resources will be recreated. The goal is to require an explicit opt-in if replacements are detected.
- Immutable subnet aliasing: Helm charts and agent configs reference subnet outputs. Replacing subnets previously required simultaneous consumer updates. By introducing alias resources that remain stable (pointing to a changing subnet_id), we allow consumers to reference aliases, enabling transparent subnet replacement without code changes.

Review thread (high-level):
- Ari: "I like the approach but we need stronger guardrails in the plan-checker to avoid accidental replacements in CI; can we add an allowlist opt-in and a clearer exit code?"
- Author reply: "Added an allowlist flag and exit codes. Plan-checker now emits a machine-readable report in addition to human text."
- Diego: "Tenant-proxy role looks okay but ensure the AssumeRole duration is limited and audit annotations are emitted."
- Author reply: "Set duration to 15m by default and added CloudTrail-friendly tags for tenant/upgrade-id."
- Samir: "Can we make the drain-agent optional for lightweight on-prem installs?"
- Author reply: "Yes, module flag 'enable_drainer' defaults to true for safety but can be toggled; updated examples to show minimal footprint installation."

CI and testing:
- CI job "tf-modules/validate" runs terraform fmt, tflint, and the new plan-checker in dry-run mode.
- Integration job "private-integration/gpu-upgrade-sim" spins up a tiny test cluster in test account and runs the drain-agent smoke test (flake observed once, retried).
- Final CI status: all checks passed after plan-checker tweaks.

Migration path and docs:
- examples/private-migration/README.md contains a step-by-step that: 1) run plan-checker against current state (dry-run) 2) fix issues (allowlist or refactor) 3) apply mapping with backup of tfstate 4) run small controlled upgrade using gpu-node-lifecycle broker 5) validate workloads and rollback if needed
- Included a sample 'rollback playbook' that uses subnet-alias remapping to re-point consumers to previous subnet alias.

Rollout and risk:
- This change is additive: modules are optional and existing terraform compositions remain unchanged by default.
- The primary risk is operator error during manual opt-in of mapping when plan-checker reports replacements; mitigations: explicit opt-in flags, pre-migration backups, and a read-only dry-run mode in CI.

Merge and follow-ups:
- Squash-merged to main.
- Follow-ups tracked: ENG-1372 (add e2e for multi-tenant migration), ENG-1380 (helm chart update to consume subnet-alias outputs), ENG-1391 (operator-facing dashboard for active upgrades).

Summary: This PR provides a practical, incrementally-adoptable path to safer GPU nodepool upgrades and state boundary evolution for private deployments. It reduces the need for ad-hoc scripts and gives SREs deterministic, testable tools for migration and rollback.
